title: Lab course step
description: One screen of a lab's guided course. Files live at services/labs/<slug>/course/NN-name.md as Markdown with YAML frontmatter; this schema describes the PARSED object, not the file bytes. It is the single authority CI validates against, and the TypeScript and Go types are generated from it - never hand-written.

kind.description: Which screen shape this is. concept and quiz are the training-guide template's two; flag is the deliberate capstone screen - it takes the CTF flag captured in the live lab and marks the lab solved. The expected flag is never in content; it lives server-side in labs.Module.Flag.

ey.description: Eyebrow label, top-left, rendered uppercase. Signals the act: CONCEPT 1, FEATURE, UNDER THE HOOD, DEEP DIVE, GUT-CHECK, RECAP.

tag.description: Muted subtitle, top-right. Mutually exclusive with chip; chip wins if both are set, so setting both is rejected rather than silently resolved.

chip.description: A labelled pill, top-right, for a screen that carries weight - a severity, a key takeaway, a caveat.

tone.description: accent = a key idea; warn = caution; danger = a pitfall. Semantic only - do not pick by colour.

allOf.description: tag and chip both occupy the top-right slot. Refusing both is better than picking a winner silently.

title.description: The screen's claim, stated plainly. A title that is a topic ('Namespaces') rather than a claim ('A namespace is not a security boundary') wastes the screen.

body.description: The prose, as restricted Markdown. Backticks mark a term's first use and render as a mono chip; the cold-term lint checks every such term was introduced on an earlier screen. No raw HTML or SVG.

aha.description: The reveal. This must carry the ANALOGY or the 'so what', never more mechanics - a reveal that restates the body is the single most common way these screens go flat.

revealLabel.description: Button text for the reveal. Defaults to 'reveal the intuition'; use 'the fix', 'the takeaway', 'why it matters' when they fit better.

q.description: The question. The intuitive answer should be wrong - a quiz that confirms what the reader already assumed teaches nothing.

opts.description: 2-4 options, exactly one correct. More than four does not fit the pane and stops being a test of understanding.

explain.description: Why the intuitive answer fails and the right one holds. This is the actual teaching moment, not a footnote to it.

title.description: The capstone prompt, stated as a claim the flag proves ('You read a secret you were never meant to reach').

body.description: Restricted Markdown telling the student to paste the k8labs{...} value they captured. The expected flag is NEVER written here - it is server-side in labs.Module.Flag.

aha.description: Optional one-line reveal - why capturing this flag is the proof the technique worked.

revealLabel.description: Button text for the optional reveal.

diagram.description: A declarative drawing, compiled to SVG by the same box/wire/lbl/seal primitives the training-guide template uses. Declarative rather than a JS function on purpose: it is what lets CI check for overlapping labels, which authoring.md otherwise says can only be caught by eyeballing the page.

caption.description: One line under the drawing, rendered in the reserved y 240-270 band so it can never collide with the shapes above it.

tone.description: Semantic role, never a colour. accent = the good/verified path and the subject of the screen; warn = caution; danger = where it breaks or the attack; neutral = ordinary plumbing. More than about three tones on one drawing reads as noise.

box.description: A rounded actor box. Boxes are things.

frame.description: A container outline that other shapes sit inside - 'one cluster holding these namespaces'. Exempt from the box-overlap lint by design, since containing things is its whole job; still bounds-checked, and its caption is drawn on the border so it cannot collide with the contents.

wire.description: A connector. Wires are flow. Use dashed + danger for an attack arrow.

label.description: Free text. Not measured by the layout, so keep it short - the overlap lint estimates its box from the character count and will reject a long one that lands on a shape.

seal.description: A wax-seal glyph: intact (a check) or broken (a crack). The house way to say 'this held' or 'this shattered'.

delay.description: Animation start, in seconds. Stagger left-to-right ~0.15-0.3s apart so the drawing assembles as the idea builds.
